Subject: Sizing + perf/$ breakdown for Orion reserved pool — proposal and discount tiers

Hi Olivia,

Thanks again for the deep dive on Friday. Attached is an initial commercial and sizing proposal for the Orion dedicated pool. Below is the short version with the perf/$ tradeoffs we discussed — I focused on three candidate shapes so your infra and product teams can weigh memory vs throughput vs unit cost.

High-level: Orion wants predictable throughput for chat (low-latency) and cheaper bulk embedding throughput for nightly jobs. We recommend a small latency tier (H100) + larger throughput tier (L40S/A100 mixed) with an optional memory-heavy A100-80GB class for some stateful models.

GPU candidates (summary perf/$):
- H100-80GB (low-latency chat): ~1.0x baseline latency for autoregressive workloads, ~2.2x peak tokens/sec vs A100-40 for short sequences; est. list cost $7.80/hr (hosted-equivalent). Perf/$: best for latency-critical paths.
- A100-80GB (memory heavy): ~0.9x tokens/sec vs H100 on some kernels but much larger KV memory headroom for long-context models; list $5.25/hr. Best when you need 80GB process space per model.
- L40S-48GB (embeddings/batch infer): ~0.6x tokens/sec vs A100 but ~40–50% lower list cost ($2.90/hr). Best for high-throughput, low-memory workloads (embeddings, rerank).

Recommended pool archetype for Orion (proposal):
- Latency pool: 6 x H100-80GB (pin for chat endpoints)
- Memory pool: 4 x A100-80GB (for long-context experiments and stateful sessions)
- Throughput pool: 12 x L40S-48GB (bulk embeddings, batching)

Commit & discounts (provisional):
- 12-month reserved commit: 18% discount on list pool rates + 10% committed burst credit for first 3 months
- 6-month commit: 12% discount, smaller onboarding credit
- Pilot (no long-term commit): 4-week trial with committed baseline (1 month-equivalent invoice) and pilot discount applied, then convert to reserved for a credit against the first invoice.

Throughput guarantees and fallbacks:
- We can guarantee baseline throughput with autoscaling headroom within the dedicated pool. SLA target for provisioned pool: 99.9% availability for allocated vCPU/GPU time.
- We propose automatic routing to compatible hosted variants (Redwood-hosted H100/A100) for short bursts beyond committed capacity — this costs the on-demand rate plus a 10% premium.

Open items I need from you to finalize numbers:
1) Typical average sequence length for chat (tokens) and 99th percentile sequence length
2) Target p95 latency for chat (ms) we should design to meet
3) Weekend/nightly embedding batch window and peak concurrency for bulk jobs

Attached: a one-page pricing summary, the raw benchmark CSV we ran against your sample prompts, and a commit-tier sheet with granular line items.

If this looks directionally right I can convert into a formal SOW and a one-page mutual action plan for signatures.

Best,
Camila Reyes

Subject: Re: Sizing + perf/$ breakdown for Orion reserved pool — proposal and discount tiers

Thanks Camila — this is a great starting point. A few clarifying questions so we can review with eng/finance tomorrow: 

- For the H100 latency pool: we primarily need p95 chat latency < 250ms for 1–4 shot prompts with ~1k token context. Does the H100 configuration above assume KV-cache pinning per-session?
- For A100 vs H100: can you give an example workload (model + batch size) where A100-80GB materially outperforms H100 for memory-heavy workloads? Our research engineer wants to understand threshold points where A100 is cheaper overall.
- On commit sizing: finance would prefer a tiered commit where we can start with 25% of the proposed pool and ramp to 100% over 8–12 weeks — can Redwood support a staged ramp with pro-rata pricing/credits?

Finally — is there an option to add short-term burst capacity (2–3 weeks) at a fixed uplift (so we don't face unpredictable overage charges) while we test?

Appreciate it — I'll loop in our eng lead if needed.

—Olivia
Director of Platform | Orion AI
olivia.park@orion.ai

Subject: Fwd: Sizing + perf/$ breakdown for Orion reserved pool — clarifications from Olivia

Ben/Karthik — FYI, Olivia asked for staged ramp, example A100 wins, and a predictable burst uplift for 2–3 weeks. Draft response below and proposed commercial play. Thoughts?

DRAFT (to send to Orion):
- H100 config: we assume KV-cache pinned per-session; the latency numbers include a small routing buffer and continuous batching disabled for chat endpoints. p95 < 250ms is achievable with 6 H100s for their expected concurrency (per their earlier notes), but we should validate with a 48–72 hour soak test.
- A100 example: for our LLM-ctx-32k-style workload (dense embeddings + long context), A100-80GB avoids frequent KV evictions and reduces repeat kernel overhead — we saw 12–18% lower tail latency and 8–12% lower cost for large-batch generation in our benchmarks. Will attach the specific CSV slices.
- Staged ramp: offer a 3-step ramp: 25% commit for weeks 1–4, 60% for weeks 5–8, 100% thereafter across a 12-week window. Pro-rata invoices each month; we convert pilot credit against first reserved invoice.
- Burst uplift: offer a capped burst pool at +15% capacity for up to 21 days at a fixed uplift of +20% on list rates. This keeps finance happy and avoids open-ended overages.

Commercial recommendation (our side):
- Convert to a 12-month reserved with the staged ramp and the 21-day capped burst option. Negotiate a final discount of 18% at full commit, sliding prorata at ramp steps (8% at 25%, 12% at 60%). Include 2-week onboarding and a 1-day soak test during which we can instrument p95/p99.

Please comment quickly — Orion is waiting for a customer-facing note.

Camila

Hi Olivia / team,

Thanks for the questions — we've incorporated them and are proposing the following formal offer to make ramping safe for you and predictable for finance: 

Offer (final, subject to SOW):
- Pool composition (provisioned): 6 H100-80GB (latency), 4 A100-80GB (memory), 12 L40S-48GB (throughput).
- Commitment: 12 months, staged ramp: 25% (wk1–4), 60% (wk5–8), 100% (wk9+). Discounts: 8% @25%, 12% @60%, 18% @100% applied to pool list rates.
- Burst: capped burst allowance up to +15% of full pool for up to 21 days/year at uplift +20% on list rates (fixed).
- Pilot: 4-week pilot option (no long-term billing obligation beyond the pilot period invoice), pilot converts to reserved commitment with applied credit equal to 30% of pilot invoice if converted within 30 days.
- SLA & testing: 2-week onboarding with a 48–72hr soak test to validate p95 <250ms for chat. Contracted availability for provisioned GPUs: 99.9%.

Next steps I propose:
1) If accepted, we'll send a one-page MOU + SOW and schedule a 2-week onboarding slot in Jan.
2) Engineering: we'll run a targeted 48hr soak test using your sample payloads and share the instrumented dashboards.
3) Finance: we can put a staged SOW with clear pro-rata invoicing and a DocuSign link for signatures.

I've attached the updated pricing PDF and the commit-tiers sheet. Let me know if finance wants the fixed burst priced differently (we can flex up to +25% uplift if they prefer a lower cap).

Best,
